title: Repeated Actions and Lingering Habits (-gat/-get)
goal: I can form and interpret frequentative verbs with -gat/-get and linking-vowel variants (-ogat/-eget/-öget)
I can distinguish single/goal-oriented actions (olvas, néz, kérdez) from unhurried or repeated actions (olvasgat, nézeget, kérdezget)
I can talk about cherished family habits, heirlooms, and ancestral memory

sections.title: Unit 5: Roots, Tradition & Collective Memory
body: Hungarian verbs are extraordinarily sensitive to the rhythm, duration, and emotional warmth of an action. Through derivational suffixes such as -gat/-get and -dogál/-degél/-dögél, speakers distinguish between reading a book straight through (olvas), paging through it at leisure over winter evenings (olvasgat), and sitting quietly by the hearth lost in thought (üldögél).

In this unit, paired with Áron Tamási's Transylvanian classic Ábel a rengetegben, you will master the aspectual system of frequentative, iterative, and instantaneous verbs alongside distributive idioms of generational continuity (nemzedékről nemzedékre, évről évre).
